steps.body: A square garden with area 81 sq ft has a side length that solves side² = 81 — since a physical length can't be negative, only the POSITIVE solution makes sense here: side = 9 ft. Real-world root problems often drop the negative solution for exactly this reason.

widget.prompt: A square rug has an area of 36 square feet. What is its side length, in feet? Set the side until the square covers 36.
widget.lowFeedback: That square covers less than 36 square feet. Widen the side and watch the area climb.
widget.highFeedback: That square covers more than 36 square feet. Each extra foot of side adds a whole strip.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents roots context.
invariants: The manipulated model and the mathematical relationship for roots context must stay consistent.
misconceptions: Changing a visible feature without preserving the relationship that defines roots context.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same mathematical relationship?

predict.prompt: A square rug covers 36 square feet. Its side length is…
predict.reveal: 6 feet, because 6 × 6 = 36. Halving gives 18, which would be right if area were side + side — but area is side TIMES side, so undoing it takes a square root rather than a halving.

steps.body: A cube-shaped box with volume 125 cubic inches has an edge length that solves edge³ = 125 — and since cube equations have only ONE real solution anyway, there's no sign ambiguity to resolve here: edge = 5 in.

explanationVariants: edge³ = 27, and 3³ = 27, so the edge length is 3 cm.

widget.prompt: A cube-shaped block has a volume of 27 cubic centimeters. What is its edge length, in centimeters?

commonErrors.feedback: That's a third of 27, not its cube root — 3³ = 27, so the edge is 3 cm.
That's half of 27, not a cube root — check 3³ = 27 instead.

widget.fallbackFeedback: edge³ = 27, and 3³ = 27, so the edge length is 3 cm.

widget.prompt: A square window has an area of 144 square inches. What is its side length, in inches?

commonErrors.feedback: That's half of 144, not its square root — 12² = 144, so the side is 12 in.
A physical side length can't be negative — use the positive solution: 12 in.

widget.fallbackFeedback: side² = 144, and 12² = 144, so the side is 12 in.

steps.body: Distinguish which root the context needs.
explanationVariants: A square area problem needs side² = p, solved with a square root; a cube volume problem needs edge³ = p, solved with a cube root.
Area is 2-dimensional (length × length, so squared); volume here is 3-dimensional (length × length × length, so cubed).

widget.prompt: A cube-shaped tank has a volume of 64 cubic meters. Which equation finds its edge length e?

options.label: e³ = 64
options.feedback: Right — volume is 3-dimensional, so the edge is cubed.

options.label: e² = 64
options.feedback: That's the equation for an AREA problem, not volume — volume needs e³=64.

options.label: e × 3 = 64
options.feedback: Volume isn't edge times 3 — it's edge cubed (edge×edge×edge).

options.label: e = 64
options.feedback: That skips the cubing relationship entirely — the correct equation is e³=64.

explanationVariants: side² = 100, and 10² = 100, so the side length is 10 m.
The positive square root of 100 is 10.

widget.prompt: A square field has an area of 100 square meters. What is its side length, in meters?

commonErrors.feedback: That's half of 100, not its square root — 10² = 100, so the side is 10 m.
A physical side length can't be negative — use the positive solution: 10 m.

widget.fallbackFeedback: side² = 100, and 10² = 100, so the side is 10 m.

explanationVariants: Volume is 3-dimensional, so edge³ = 216; since 6³ = 216, the edge length is 6 ft.
Set up edge³ = 216 (volume, cubic), then solve: 6³ = 216.

widget.prompt: A cube-shaped crate has a volume of 216 cubic feet. What is its edge length, in feet?

commonErrors.feedback: That's a third of 216, not its cube root — 6³ = 216, so the edge is 6 ft.
That's a sixth of 216, and also 6² rather than 6³ — check 6×6×6 = 216.

widget.fallbackFeedback: edge³ = 216, and 6³ = 216, so the edge length is 6 ft.

hints: Volume is length × length × length — set up edge³ = 216.
Look for a perfect cube close to 216 (try 5³, 6³, 7³…).
6³ = 216, so the edge length is 6 ft.

steps.body: Match the equation to the dimension: area problems square, volume problems cube.
takeaways: A physical length is always positive, so real-world square-root problems use only the positive solution.
Area (2D) problems set up side² = p; volume (3D) problems set up edge³ = p.
Cube-root context problems never have a sign ambiguity to resolve, since x³=p has just one real solution.
